title: Cleanliness and dignity around urine, bladder, and bowel changes

source_packet.source_basis: Public-source practice-layer synthesis for schema testing; no private testimony, no contributor interview, no claim of corpus completeness.
limitations: Public sources describe recognized care patterns but do not supply firsthand room texture.
This record must not become procedure-level instruction for a particular death.
Treatment, legal, ritual, emergency, and equipment decisions remain local and must be handled by qualified teams or relevant authorities.

moment.plain_scene: Urine becomes less frequent or darker, incontinence happens, or the bladder and bowel become part of the room; carers try to preserve cleanliness without shame.

content_layers.observation_text: Public sources describe less urine, bladder and bowel changes, and possible release near death; the practice layer frames these as dignity and care-team matters rather than embarrassment.
content_layers.source_synthesis: The source set supports cautious observation and dignity language. It does not support family-level catheter, bowel, or body-care instruction without local guidance.

interpretation.editor_interpretation: This record makes the unpretty ordinary. It is necessary because shame can enter the room faster than knowledge, especially around smell, linens, and cleanup.

what_this_is_not: not a catheter or bowel-care manual
not an instruction for after-death body handling where professionals or local law should guide
uncertainties: Bowel/bladder changes vary with illness, medicines, hydration, equipment, and setting.
Cultural and personal modesty preferences matter.
Future professional records should include aides and nurses, who often hold the practical knowledge.
content_layers.lay_orientation: A lay surface should make clear that bladder and bowel changes can happen and do not erase dignity, while routing cleanup/equipment questions to carers or local services.
content_layers.practitioner_notes: A practitioner surface should collect privacy, linen, catheter, smell, and family-language scripts without turning them into unreviewed procedure.
language_notes: Name smell only as needed, without disgust language.

provenance.provenance_statement: Drafted from named public sources to test the practice layer. It should be reviewed before any public surface uses it.

safety.clinical_boundary: This record is observational/source-indexing only. It is not medical advice, not a prognosis, not a legal instruction, not a ritual authority, and not a substitute for a local hospice, clinician, emergency, legal, cultural, or care team.
safety.safety_notes: Before public use, route through clinical or domain review and ensure any lay surface directs urgent, worried, legal, medication, swallowing, equipment, or body-handling questions to qualified local support.
